utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Nice: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: B-071, yesterday we started to look at a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can it now be produced. It's going to be Exhibit 336/71A. And if the Chamber has it in the same form that I have, it's copied on two sides. It's an extract from our standard atlas, with markings by the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very swiftly, because I don't want to take unnecessary time when you've given the evidence orally, does this map show, starting on the first side at number 1 near Mrkonjic, the various places where you were held: First, Mrkonjic Grad; then the second place marked, hard to read just to the south of Trnovo; the third place to the north of that, the fourth place up on the right-hand side at Prnjavor; and then over the page, the fifth place, Derventa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 10, page 4. I asked you yesterday about senior soldiers visiting the barracks Zdravko Pcelar at Derventa.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Think back and tell us of the most senior generals that you saw visit there by name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember Momir Talic, Slavko Lisica - the former Major Lisica Slavko - Bosko Pejovic, lieutenant colonel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember any other generals who visited there, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember, but I've just forgotten just now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the summer of 1995, paragraph 11, were people cleaning the streets in Derventa town to which, as you told us yesterday, you had general access? Were you there by coincidence when an event happened involving Arkan's military policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that? What happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I left the barracks compound to have a walk, people were cleaning the streets, and I was there when Arkan's army turned up. I just noticed a Chevrolet, a black one, and they were taking -- collecting up people from the street, and they were deserters, looking for deserters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were taken in the direction of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you included in those who were picked up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You having no papers on you at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having been picked up in that way, what happened to you? Were you put to work in a unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Could you repeat that, please, for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When Arkan's army collected us up, we worked for Arkan's army. We went to the battlefront, carried ammunition, helped in the kitchen, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the name of the unit of which you were now a member was what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serb Volunteer Guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a unit by the name of Partizaneri?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was a work obligation unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you work in that unit or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a uniform provided at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I had a camouflage uniform but without any insignia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And no beret and no weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you paid at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After a short time in Prijedor, were you relocated or located to the area of Mrkonjic Grad and the village of Mala Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness can now have on the overhead projector Exhibit 336/71B, another marked page from our standard atlas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does this marked map, marked by you, show movements of Arkan's Tigers starting at Derventa, moving to Prijedor, and then we can see further down Mrkonjic Grad, so that we've covered the first three locations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your knowledge of and experience of Arkan's units enabled you to tell us, please, how they were divided. What were the subdivisions of his paramilitary formation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for example, he had a special purposes unit. Then he had his tank people and the artillery, mortars and snipers, professional ones. And he had intervention units, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a military police unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They wore black uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A reconnaissance unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And a communications unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The ranks used by Arkan's Tigers, were they similar to or different from the normal military ranks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, mostly they were different ranks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To what other military organisation did the ranks in his formation most correspond?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like, for example, the army of Republika Srpska but different names. They were called differently. For example, lance corporals in the Srpska Republika army was a corporal in his army. That was the name of the ranks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever likened the formation of Arkan's unit to any foreign military force?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. There were some others there, other insignia, like the Eagles and the Milicija, militia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. As to uniforms, you've told us about the camouflage uniforms. Were they NATO in style?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The officers, what colour were their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They wore camouflage uniforms in two parts. Two-piece.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any solid-colour uniforms, uniforms of a single colour worn?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were green uniforms with the garrison, and they were the tank unit soldiers that wore them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the officers wear when they were not on active manoeuvre? What colour uniforms did they wear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Camouflage NATO uniforms, two-piece, red berets, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What colour berets did the ordinary soldiers and non-commissioned ranks wear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The non-commissioned officers wore red with black berets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were soldiers and officers equipped with automatic weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The soldiers having what kind of weapons, typically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the type of weapon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Snipers, Hecklers, Scorpios, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The officers usually had what type of weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Automatic weapons and pistols.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any particular make of automatic weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they did have some weapons, but I'm not well-versed in the types of weapons. F-16, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there military jeeps available?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer. We're finding it difficult to follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Could you repeat the answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were mostly all civilian cars, but they were just painted the black.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any jeeps that you can recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With a tiger on the door. Pajero jeeps, Nissan, Mercedes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any accounts of where these vehicles that Arkan's units used had come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all taken from the surroundings of Vukovar. Slavonski Brod, Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were Arkan's men divided within themselves as between Tigers and something called Super Tigers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were the Tigers? Who were the Super Tigers? What defined them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tigers were ordinary Tigers from 1992 onwards, whereas the Super Tigers were from 1991, from the attacks on Slavonia, and they had different patches on their sleeves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did some of those men tell you about operations they'd been on? Did they say where they'd been in operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in Bosnia, but they spoke about Erdut and Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you anything about operations in Bosnia, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They spoke of Bosanski Samac, Bijeljina, Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've described --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- remember any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... because that's where the vehicles came from. In telling you of these operations, did the soldiers concerned say anything about whether people had been killed in the course of these operations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in Bosnia. They didn't make any mention of any such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they make any such mention of any such things in any other such places?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Vukovar, when we came to Erdut.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Super Tigers appear to have privileges over and above the ordinary Tigers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had different documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have any other privileges about when they had to parade and matters of that sort?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't have to line up. They would come to the camp compound drunk. They would harass the other soldiers. If someone made a mistake, he would be disciplined by being beaten with a truncheon, tied to a lamppost, poured water over them in the middle of winter, and things like that. Those were the measures of discipline.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Tigers and Super Tigers, can you look, please, at this exhibit which will be on the screen, Exhibit 349, tab 2 and tab 8. Do you recognise if that's -- that's tab 2, yes. Do you recognise that patch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the patch of the Serbian Volunteer Guards. This was borne by regular soldiers from 1992 onwards. And this also is a Tiger patch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can we look --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, the previous one, was that tab 2 or tab 3?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Tab 3. I'm grateful. Previously tendered through B-1738. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If the witness can tell the difference between tab 4 and tab 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can you bring up tab 4, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is tab 4, and then tab 8, please. What's the difference between --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. Tab 8. A tiger but different colour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one minute, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is tab 4, and this is tab 8.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Tiger patches, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The difference is in the colour. And these were worn by the Super Tigers. They're different in colour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: His Honour may want to know which one, or was it both -- if only one, which one was worn by the Super Tigers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the other one? Go back to the other one, please. And was this one worn by --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was worn by Tigers who joined from 1992 and onwards.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: They haven't got the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Yesterday I got instruction to press the button here. [Interpretation] I understand that this is a protected witness, among other things by voice distortion, but I wish to draw attention to the fact that the distortion is such, is so extreme, that his speech is totally incomprehensible, and that is why, as you see, the interpreters are having a problem too. So could the technical department distort the voice in such a way that he is -- that he is comprehensible? We are just hearing muttering noises.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: He doesn't have voice distortion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There's no voice distortion, I'm told, in his case. We'll try and get the witness to speak as clearly as he can, and we'll put -- yes, put the second microphone on. If you put his second microphone on, it may help.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness perhaps move away from the microphone just a little bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is suggested is that you move a bit further from the microphone. Could you move a bit further away. We'll see how we get on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Concluding the patches for the time being, did they wear different patches on each shoulder?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this one -- we'll move to the next one. And that one would be on the same soldier but on different sides of his body; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just going back to one topic: You were telling us about the cars that were available to Arkan's men, a black car with a tiger on the door. Did you ever travel in such a car yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but mostly in vans and jeeps. And all these vehicles had certain markings on them. Only the official vehicle used by Arkan had no markings on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these marked vehicles, did you ever travel with them across the border of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I travelled in a kombi van.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any difficulties in crossing that border, or was it easy to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no problems. Arkan's guards had an advantage everywhere. They could move around Republika Srpska, Vukovar, Serbia. The way they behaved, they could go around anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The jeeps, where was it said that they had come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. Could you explain, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You've told us where the cars came from, but where did the jeeps -- you've now told us there were jeeps. Where had those jeeps come from? Where had they been obtained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Belgrade mostly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. B-071, you have produced in your statement and now reproduced as a separate exhibit a list of Tigers by name where you know the name, or a part name where you only know part of the name. That is tab 1 in this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exhibit 416.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the list itself, which can be placed on the overhead projector, there's no problem with that, is of 93 names. There's a colour-coded version which I have. Can we place the English version on the overhead projector? And can we provide a B/C/S version to the witness, Usher, please. Your Honour, I'm going to read out from the list about 20 names in order that they can be on the LiveNote record not least for searching purposes but also because they're important names. utterances.text: B-071, have you identified from this general list of names --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- those who are or were to your knowledge Super Tigers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: And finally 91, Igor whose full name you didn't know but he was also known as Trubac?

utterances.text: And those are the Super Tigers, and then there are just six other names --

utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 28, was there a Tiger known as Legija from the French Foreign Legion, an instructor who runs a discotheque, or did at the time of your statement, Zambi in Belgrade, and had a tattoo of a rose on the right side of his neck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 37, a man known as Suca or Suco who was present in Erdut and was a sniper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Over the page to 62, a man called Nikola Saponja, born in Mostar, one of Arkan's bodyguards --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- karate champion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And his brother Miroslav Saponja was involved in the security or construction staff in Belgrade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 65, Mile Ulemek, from Dalj, head of the communications unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally number 75, Goran Bozovic, also known as Raja, who had a position with the state security and was a frequent visitor to Arkan at his party headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: B-071, with an eye to the exhibit showing the movement of Arkan's men, were you in September 1995 relocated from Prijedor to Mala Manjaca near Mrkonjic Grad, and was it there that you saw Arkan on an occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all soldiers lined up and did he address them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Roughly how many Tigers were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: His unit numbered 1.000 and a little over, men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this occasion, what did he say to his men, did he talk about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived in Mrkonjic, he said that Jasenova Kosa had to be captured and that that same day they had to move on to the front. A feature had to be captured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Was there another unit there as well as his Tigers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw a unit with "milicija" on their sleeves, wearing blue camouflage uniforms and some with round patches like White Eagles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Arkan speaking to the commanders of those two other units; and if so, who appeared to be in charge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appeared to me that Arkan was the main boss and that everyone was listening to his orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we look now, please, at Exhibit 349, tab 10. What is this the patch of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The White Eagles.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the operation that Arkan had spoken of, your function was to do what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My mistake. What were you doing in the course of the operation of which Arkan spoke? What job did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I carried ammunition where necessary. For instance, grenades for mortars. And I carried food. And this was packed food from NATO, the kind of food that the UN soldiers in Bosnia are using.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 3rd of October of 1995, did something happen to one of Arkan's Tigers, Djordje Djekic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was killed there in Perici. That's the name of the location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were three opposing soldiers captured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see what happened to one of those soldiers at the hands of a Tiger called Glisa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He caught him, stripped him to his underwear, hit him with his rifle butt on his legs and eventually he stuck his bayonet into his back, and he left him there lying in the yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that man die?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what happened to him. He was lying there on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you shown a knife afterwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He showed me that knife. There was an inscription on it. As far as I can remember, it said "Ivo Bakovic" on it, and he asked me whether I knew the man, and I said no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that apparently the man who had been knifed in the back by Glisa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What ethnicity was the man who had been knifed in the back by Glisa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was a Muslim or a Croat, because he would take the documents immediately and hand them over to the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the following day, was Arkan informed of the death of his soldier Djordje Djekic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were two captured soldiers brought to the village of Peric in Mrkonjic Grad when Arkan arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to those two captured soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One survived and the other one, when Arkan got out of his jeep, he took out his pistol and shot him in the head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 5th of October of 1995, did Arkan's unit suffer some losses in the battle, and were you injured yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you taken to barracks at Mladen Stojanovic in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you discover the seriously wounded Tigers were taken for treatment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were taken to Serbia for treatment, those who lost a leg or an arm and had other serious injuries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they taken by helicopter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've spoken already of Arkan's discipline in part. I think you mentioned people being tied to a flagpole and beaten. Did he employ solitary confinement as punishment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For instance, there were cases that people would be shut up for three days as punishment, without being given food or water. It all depended on the punishment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at ordinary eating times, were soldiers allowed to talk one to another or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Arkan himself ever physically hit or slap people under his apparent command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would happen that he would come angry, nervous. He would lose in gambling and then he would slap an officer, a non-commissioned officer, out of fury.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can we now move, as I think you did, to Erdut. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We look at the map that you have yourself drawn, tab 2. For future reference or for this reference, does this map show us the location of the Erdut centre --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- in juxtaposition with the kiosk and the gas station, the sugar refinery, and the road to Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's for future reference, if helpful. When you arrived in Erdut, were you recovering from your wounds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hadn't recovered fully. I stayed in Vukovar for two or three days in order to recover.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But -- and in Erdut, how many Tigers were there there when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived, there weren't that many. About 300 soldiers, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there one incident that you were involved in concerning a well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've drawn a map of this, a redacted form of which may go on the overhead projector and is tab 3. While that's being made available, what was your job at the well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My task was to cover up the well with earth and to cover it up with branches so as to conceal it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was one of the men working there Radomir Trojanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he tell you of the well, why you were covering it up and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wondering why we were doing this, and he said it was a mass grave formed there in Vukovar and that we had to conceal it so it wouldn't be noticeable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say a mass grave formed there in Vukovar, containing people killed where? Killed in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably they were residents of Vukovar or maybe Erdut, Dalj, the places around there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say from what year or years these bodies had come, when they'd been killed?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can see the map again for reference. It's some distance from Erdut, and the way you've marked it, it's south and east of the Danube River. There's corn fields. You've identified where the soil came from, and you've identified a house with some evergreen trees and other features. How near to or far from the nearest village or town was this well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a village right there, and this was the house in the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the village was the village of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Radomir Trojanovic told you about these bodies coming from Vukovar in 1991. Did other Tigers or Super Tigers tell you of previous wartime experiences?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for example, they would come drunk and recount stories of how they killed people around Vukovar, and children weren't spared either. They did everything they shouldn't have done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In March of 1996, did the Tigers of Arkan leave Erdut and go to Djeletovci?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when there, were they stationed beside or together with the forces of another group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was another group there, and they were the Skorpios.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they were under the command of whom? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ljuba Mauzer, as I heard it, a man called Ljuba Mauzer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He came from which town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the Skorpions similar in their discipline and equipment to the Tigers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They had the same uniform. It was a camouflage NATO uniform, two pieces, and overalls with the two zips.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they seem to be similarly disciplined and controlled to the way in which Arkan's Tigers were disciplined and controlled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we could conclude that. They weren't allowed to get drunk. They weren't allowed to do what they weren't supposed to do. They would have to line up to get food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. When the Tigers left Erdut, was there any looting by them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They would take windows and doors from houses, for example, everything that could be used. Everything would be taken out and loaded up onto trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those trucks took the looted property where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were taken off towards Serbia, to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know to which particular location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it was close to Belgrade. They had a warehouse there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was one of the Tigers Veliki Rambo who you've already spoken of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the main -- in charge of the mines in Arkan's team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he do when property at Erdut was looted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He occupied the weekend homes of people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Did Arkan's Tigers finally withdraw to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you now given a military booklet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when I came to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you carry on working for Arkan? If so, where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked in his bakery called the Golden Crown or Zlatna Kruna, across the road from the stadium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get paid or did you just get accommodation and food?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was paid the first two months, but afterwards I was just given food and lodging.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1997, did Arkan ask for your military booklet back, and everybody else's?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he make another request of you and of others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for example, he asked -- he came to us nicely at his party headquarters and asked whether we would like to go to the Republika Srpska or whether we preferred to remain in Yugoslavia. And depending on the decision people made, some people left, some people stayed. I decided to go back to Republika Srpska to see what had happened to my relatives. Then he took my military booklet, gave me a driver, and said, "Well, go to Doboj then."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you taken home or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took me to Doboj, drove me to Doboj, and the Kamenolom, the prison there. It was a civilian prison at the quarry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you then detained in that prison rather than being taken home as had been arranged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that prison, were you or did you in due course sign a piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had to sign a piece of paper testifying that I had committed a murder, that I had killed a man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any truth in that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About one year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Escaping in due course with the assistance of a guard, I think?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on escape, were you able to walk home to Banja Luka? Or walk to Banja Luka, in any event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I arrived at Banja Luka and Crna Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a few more questions, B-071. In Erdut, did you notice the type of visitors that Arkan received and where they came from, as judged by their car registration plates?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would come -- for example, cars would come. There were some Audis, the dark type of Audi car. And then the people would wear civilian clothes, suits and ties. I remember one such man. There were some diplomatic registration plates or the BG, Belgrade licence plates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Paragraph 27. While you were in Djeletovci, did you form some conclusions from your observations about whether Arkan had any connections with the Belgrade DB?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for example, on one occasion when we were going back from Djeletovci where we cut down the forest for Arkan's bridge there, we encountered two policemen. They were wearing uniforms. And at that -- and we were stopped and asked whether we had anything to do with the commander because he had a package for the commander. He took up his Motorola and called 99, which was their commander's signal, the connection, communication, and he sent two vehicles and took off -- took away the package towards Djeletovci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you also aware of an incident in March or April of 1996, shortly before you left for Belgrade, when there was a shipment that arrived for Arkan in a refrigerated truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people in the van -- sorry. The truck had licence plates from which country?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't see the licence plates, but from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. The people with the truck dressed in what uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them was wearing civilian clothing, a suit with a tie, and the other one was wearing the militia uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the blue uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, camouflage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did a man known as Padobranac, one of Arkan's soldiers, take possession of the shipment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He called up the headquarters over there and two vehicles turned up. He took over the consignment and took it off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the consignment turned out pretty obviously to be what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came to Djeletovci, I saw that there were -- that the weapons were protected from corrosion. There were new uniforms, and I concluded that it was probably weapons and uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at this time, B-071, was it easy or difficult to travel between Serbia and Eastern Slavonia? You've probably covered this already, but was it in fact easy or difficult to make that journey?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we would go from west -- from Western Slavonia to Serbia, there was no difficulty at the border crossings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Belgrade, did you have a couple of experiences suggesting what Arkan's contacts there were with the DB? In particular, were you once checked yourself when you didn't have your ID cards with you and was Arkan or Arkan's name able to help you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was one case when I was stopped by a police patrol on the 20 -- the 29th of November was the name of the police station. They took me off down there and asked who I was and where my documents were. I said I didn't have any documents, that I forgot them in my room and that I was working at Arkan's bakery. And then they let me go straight away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A man called Duma had similar problems. Arkan discovered about it, and did he then go and address the shift officer who'd been dealing with Duma for lack of identification, and did he smack the man, the police officer concerned, and fire him from his job?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That man, that Super Tiger who had lost a leg on the front had some problems. He asked him what had happened, and he just waved his hand, and Arkan didn't like that. He didn't like you not to answer his questions. Because there was the Super Tigers and there was a difference between the Super Tigers and Tigers. And he said he had had some problems at the police station and they hassled him there because they didn't have an ID document of any kind. And then Arkan put him into his own Chevrolet and took him off to the station. And when Duma returned, he told us that on the spot he dismissed two or three of them and slapped the others who had mistreated him or hassled him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's enough of that kind of evidence, thank you very much. You'll be asked some further questions, B-071.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Cross-examined by Mr. Milosevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. B-071, what were you, a Tiger or a Super Tiger?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question. Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you, tell me; were you a Tiger or a Super Tiger?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was neither a Tiger nor a Super Tiger. I was a partisan, as we called it, and was doing a work obligation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that at the beginning of the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, you were in a HOS uniform as a soldier, a courier, a reconnaissance man.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was wearing civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have a uniform at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I understood that you were a member of the HOS.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The TO and the HOS are not the same thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The TO and the HOS is not the same army, nor did HOS exist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking about the Croatian armed forces, HOS.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know, but it didn't exist in that year where we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me then which formation, which unit did you belong to at the time when, as you say, you entered the area which was under Serb control in order to collect information and data about the deployment of the forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was an ordinary village guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what were you a member of? Were you a member of the Territorial Defence then? Could you identify for me, please, the character of the unit to which you belonged and for which you say you were a courier and a reconnaissance man.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't a unit. It wasn't a paramilitary unit either. It was a village guard or village watch. There were just ten of us, for example, and we would stand guard in case of an attack on Mrkonjic Jezero.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you were a courier. Whose courier were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village watch, the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, a courier is somebody attached to some kind of headquarters or command or some kind of commander. You were somebody's courier. You were on a reconnaissance mission too, so who were you working for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was a reconnaissance man and courier for a man in charge and in command of the village watch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was your commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't understand your answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can't answer my question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I don't think you'll be able to answer many of my questions. On page 2 of your statement, you speak about the positions at which the Serb forces were deployed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't mention the movement of Serb forces anywhere; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, those forces of yours, the ones you were reconnaissance man for, you say courier and reconnaissance missions. So the forces you worked for and as you went on reconnaissance missions, at that time were those forces preparing an attack on Serb positions at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, why did you have to do reconnaissance missions when you yourself say that you were not looking into any troop movements, just positions? So who assigned you this task? Who told you to go on these reconnaissance missions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody gave me these tasks. I had a girlfriend in Djeletovci so I would go around to see where the Serb army was, what positions they held, what kind of weapons they held, and so on. I wasn't able to return.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You were arrested wearing civilian clothing; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you take off your uniform and put civilian clothes on; when you went on assignment or a day before or when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never had a uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never had a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you belonged to some military formation or unit, you said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't a military formation, it was an ordinary village guard's group or village watch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. When you were taken prisoner and interrogated about your activities, what did you explain to them? What did you say? Who did you belong to? What were you? Who were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't explain who I was or what I was. Everybody knew me. We were all neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They all knew you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a man there at the police station who knew me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it couldn't have been a secret for that man. He knew you, so he knew your name, he knew your ethnic affiliation, everything else; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. B-071, you say that they didn't question you and interrogate you because they knew you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was questioned at the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They asked me at the police station. Do you have -- are there any other soldiers, what weapons do you have, where's this man, where's that man?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but they knew your name and they knew where you came from because you say they knew you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one man knew me, the one that took me into custody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that person who took you into custody probably had to give your name and say who you were and what you were as you say he knew you. So why are you saying all this when you were under a false name, when the people who arrested you knew you? They knew your real name, so how could you later suddenly find yourself using a false name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said a false name when I was moved to the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, can you explain this to me, please. You were transferred to the military police as a prisoner of war, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a civilian prisoner, not a prisoner of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You were transferred as a civilian. You were arrested by a man who knew you, he handed you over to the people in the police station with all the information as to your ID, and then somebody suddenly changed your name when you were put into the hands of the military police. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. B-071, you're not telling the truth. Why don't you explain to us --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I wasn't telling the truth, I wouldn't have -- I wouldn't Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. be here, and I wouldn't waste my time here or yours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you recognise the reasons for which you were taken prisoner? Did you acknowledge them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, why did the man arrest you in the first place and take you to the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know that either?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were transferred to the prison called Stari Mlin, the old mill, and stayed there until March 1994; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then to Derventa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And yesterday, I made a note of something here when you were asked. In the prison you belonged to some military unit, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you consider yourself to be a free person? You did because you went around town, you went about various business. You said you cut wood and did some cleaning; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when I was in the army, I always did cleaning work and chopped wood. That is part of the regular duties that soldiers have to do because the soldiers don't have anybody else to do this for them. So did your duties differ in any way from the duties of other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for example, there were some soldiers who had duties around vehicles or weapons or in the kitchens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they were soldiers too, those working in the kitchen and so on. All this work is done by soldiers. I have never heard of an army having servants, although perhaps some armies do have servants now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was the unit of the army of Republika Srpska. They had officers' messes, kitchens separate for the officers and separate for the men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about officers' messes or soldiers' kitchens. What I'm asking you is the following: You yourself say that you felt free. You felt yourself to be a free man, that you could move around town and you did the normal duties that soldiers are usually assigned to do. So where - how shall I put this? - you say you were a prisoner. How was it that you were a prisoner? How were you different from others? How did you see yourself as a prisoner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had my work obligations. I had this work unit. I didn't have any weapons and so on, didn't go to the front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were privileged not to have to go to the front; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As to the other duties you had to perform, they were no different from the ones anybody else had to do; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, then, as you were arrested by a man who knew you, he knew your name, he knew your ethic affiliation and everything else, during this period of six years that you have been testifying about, did any of your relatives and relations look for you? Did the authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina look for you or the authorities of the Republic of Croatia? Did they search for you? The Red Cross or anybody else from the Republic of Croatia, from the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, or from any other part or unit? Did anyone look for you? Were you on a list of missing persons, persons taken prisoner or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That's a very long question -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We were discussing the times we'll sit today. Because we missed a quarter of an hour at the beginning, we will sit until five to two this afternoon. The break will accordingly be rather later than usual, rather after half past ten. Yes. Mr. Milosevic, if you ask long and complicated questions, people can't answer them. Now, what question would you like the witness to ask -- answer, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you on a list of prisoners of war or detainees? Did anyone look for you during that period of six years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Two questions. Two questions, Witness B-071. First of all, you were on a list of prisoners of war; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Secondly, did anybody look for you as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was looking for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My relatives; my mother and father, brother, sisters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in no danger. You said you felt free. How come that you didn't find an opportunity through some sort of an exchange that were frequent in those days, to rejoin your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For instance, when there was the exchange at Manjaca, I was transferred to Prnjavor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in Prnjavor, there was no other opportunity for you to be exchanged? You were free over there too, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no exchanges. If I had had a chance, I would have escaped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But over there you were free too, as far as I understand.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I wasn't as free to move around town as I was in Derventa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you had no documents; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, as a free person, you mostly cut wood, cleaned the compound, and worked in the kitchen. I couldn't quite note down when you mentioned the cleaning of a cell with blood in it. Which barracks was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the Kula barracks in Mrkonjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that in Mrkonjic Grad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mrkonjic Grad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was a regular barracks of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a barracks from the time of Tito's rule.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So it's a barracks that had been in existence for many years. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, was there a camp there for detainees or prisoners, or was there a police station there or a place where somebody tortured somebody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no camp. There was only the military police who interrogated people and sent them to Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anyone -- as I gather you were not badly treated, you were free, did you see anyone being tortured over there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you give us the name of a person tortured there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't like to give you a name. I'd rather not mention any names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you are duty-bound to tell us the name if you know one. Otherwise, you've made it up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for instance, Mato Tokic from Jajce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he beaten in that barracks in the room that you cleaned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was beaten up to death but he lived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. He was beaten almost to death. Do you know anyone else who was beaten up over there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a couple of others but I don't know them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you know only this one name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tokic Mato.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he's from Jajce. Is he in Jajce now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where he is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you quite sure you didn't make up this story about a cell where people were beaten in a military institution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm certain 100 per cent that it is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wouldn't say so, but we'll come to that. On page 10, you say that during your captivity -- you even mentioned the name that you used, the false name that you used. Who did you arrange with to use a false name? Because your real name was obviously known. Who gave you permission to use a false name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't ask me for documents or anything like that. He just asked me what my name was and I gave them the name that's how they registered me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're saying that they're so naive that without any documents they take what you say for granted? But nobody gave you permission to use a false name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For instance in Prnjavor or Dreventa, nobody asked you your name or where you had come from. As soon as they saw an SMB uniform, they knew you were under work obligation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who gave you that SMB uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they didn't give you a prison uniform. An SMB uniform is a military uniform, so they dressed you like a regular soldier.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I didn't have any insignia or buttons or anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Since you say that various people also used various names, who are the persons behind the names Dragoljub Coric, Miroslav Tolic, Miodrag Aksentic, Sinisa Zivkovic, Nebojsa Prijevic? Who are the persons hiding behind these names, since, according to what you say, they were also false names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Croats and Bosniaks may be hiding behind those names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you know them? Did you know their real identity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they were Croats and Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by stories, yes, and the vocabulary they use differs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, it doesn't differ. I don't think it differs either. It's only recently that I heard that there were several languages. But tell me, please, how is it possible? Did you have an explanation that in that unit of the Serbian Volunteer Guards there was a group of people, Croats and Muslims, who were given Serbian names and were hiding behind those names? Who gave them permission to do that? It's not just you, apparently, but several men who made up this whole plan that you say happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Those who were in Arkan's unit, I knew where they came from. They may have been from Serbia, from Bosnia, from Croatia. I don't know where those people came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but you say you know that they were Croats and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When we spoke, I noticed the way they speak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When and where were they captured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. We didn't talk about that, nor did they say they were captured or anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But since you spent most of your time in the company of these people, if you don't know their identity or anything that might -- do you know anything that might indicate where they came from, what they did before the conflict started? Surely people talk amongst themselves. You must know something more about them. You could have learnt something about them that might have pointed to their identity. What do you know about those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything specific about them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know anything specific about the people you associated with, but you do know everything about Arkan, the Tigers and the Super Tigers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't engage in any conversations as to --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, answer this logical question at least: If you had been captives, should there have been an agreement among you if anyone was released or manages to escape that he should inform families about the others, that they were alive and where they were? Did you have any such arrangement amongst yourselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember the name of Senad Zahirovic who was also captured and was under work obligation, and he fled to Croatia, and I told him to find my family, to tell them that I was alive and where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the real identity of all of those persons, you only know of Senad Zahirovic from Zenica. Among all those persons, you only know of him. And what was the name that he used over there? Did he use his real name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wait a moment. I listed a number of names that you say were Croats and Bosniaks and have Serb names, but for this one that you knew, you don't know which name he used.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a regular JNA soldier when the war started in Derventa, and he stayed behind in the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he with you in Arkan's group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was under work obligation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a member of the Serbian Volunteer Guard like you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean a member; as a combatant or as a worker?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You're putting that the witness was a member of the Serbian Volunteer Guard. I thought he was a member of the Partizans. I may be wrong about that. Let's get it right from him. Were you also a member of the Serbian Volunteer Guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I wasn't a member of the Serb Volunteer Guard. I was a Partizaner in this work unit.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, the witness himself claims that he had an ID card of the Serbian Volunteer Guard issued in his name, this name he used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's hear about that. We haven't heard about that. We've heard about a booklet, but we haven't heard about that. Did you have a work card from the Serbian Volunteer Guard, issued in the name which you assumed? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. In Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, and Western Slavonia, I didn't have one, but in Belgrade I was given a military booklet with the inscription Serbian Volunteer Guard on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, this military booklet of the Serbian Volunteer Guard that you had as a personal ID, is it the same as any other military booklet of members of that guard -- those guards, or was yours different from the others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the same booklet. Same colour and everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So you had the same booklet as the other soldiers of the Serbian Volunteer Guards. Since you mentioned this Senad Zahirovic from Zenica, after 1998, when you managed to go home to Jajce, did you have any contact with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any contact with any other member of this unit of yours with whom you had spent so many years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I didn't see anyone in Jajce, because it's mostly inhabited by Muslims and Croats. There were no Serbs there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far -- according to what you say, you joined this Serbian Volunteer Guard, Arkan's unit, in 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from 1995, you moved around wherever Arkan's Serbian Volunteer Guards unit went? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And since you were in those guards from 1995 and moved around with it everywhere, you're still claiming that you were a captive; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you even had an ID of the unit, and you still claim that you were a captive.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that I got those documents only once I reached Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll adjourn now. It's now time to take the adjournment. We'll adjourn for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. B-071, a moment ago we established that you could not remember the names of those persons that you worked with nor their identity. So please tell me, how is it possible that you can remember almost a hundred people that were read out to you from a list that you remembered allegedly? Who gave you this list?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one gave it to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you just remembered all those names on the basis of your own memory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent two years with them, so it's normal that I know everything about them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how then can you not remember about these other people that I asked you about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe these other men have false names too. I just know them by their name and nickname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If you remember all those people so well on the basis of your own memory; for instance, on page 6 of your statement, under 29, you mention a certain Macak, whose nickname was Macak or the cat. And you say that he was one of the leading commanders of Arkan's who is now serving a prison sentence of 13 years. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. B-071, that this same Macak that you referred to is in prison ever since the end of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you claim that on the basis of what you remembered in 1995, you were able to say that he was one of the top commanders and everything else that you said. That's why I'm asking you who gave you the list.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were all officers or men who used their names or nicknames, but what name hid behind those names, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you understand that what I'm asking you about shows that this is not possible, because the man has been in prison since 1993? So you could not put him on the list.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I saw a photograph on the wall in the room where Arkan's men slept.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that that man, in 1993, was convicted by the Yugoslav courts for armed robbery carried out somewhere in the territory of Serbia, in the north, and that he's been in prison ever since?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the very fact -- this very fact shows that no one, and therefore even Arkan's men, could not be spared of criminal responsibility when there was any evidence of such crimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. No. The witness says he was there. Now, you say something different. You can give evidence about it in due course, but at the moment, that's what the witness says. You can't ask any questions based on your supposition.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not a supposition, Mr. May, but a fact, because he identifies a man in 1995 who's been in prison since 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You can call evidence about it. You will give evidence yourself in due course, but you're not doing so now. You're asking questions, and you've heard what the witness says. He identifies this man as one of Arkan's top commanders. Whether he was in prison before then, of course, is a matter, no doubt, we can be informed about.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the point, Mr. May. I'm asking questions in connection with false allegations being made here by this witness, and I think it is quite a legitimate question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
