utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. B-071, you claim that you wore the same uniforms as the rest of Arkan's soldiers. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but without any insignia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you wore the same uniforms as the others.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 10, and you mentioned something to that effect today too, in your statement you say that Arkan's forces, on the 5th of October, 1995, suffered serious losses in battles at Jasenova Kosa, close to Mrkonjic Grad; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who were those forces fighting against?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Either the HVO or the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. The forces of the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In Croatia, the Croatian Defence Council or the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on that day, as you say in your statement, you yourself were wounded; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You claim that you were injured by a grenade shrapnel at a gas station at a place near Peric; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you were not a member of the armed formations, how come you were where the fighting was at all? Because according to my information, near the gas station in Perici, there was a battle position, combat position of one of the units. Is that true or not? Just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's where the feature was, and that's where his vehicles were stationed, that's where the soldiers slept and all the rest of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And is it true that you yourself then were at these combat positions and that you took part in the fighting that went on and the fighting that that unit took part in too? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I carried ammunition and food, but I had no weapons with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true that as an injured person, you were treated identically, in the same way that all the other people were that belonged to the units, this particular unit, in fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that you shared a hospital room with Marinko Marinovic, Goran Pirocanac, someone nicknamed Bagi, Gluscevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with a certain Hans; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were together with them as somebody wounded. When Arkan's forces withdrew on October the 10th, you withdrew with them and were transferred to Erdut; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you claim you were a captive. You keep saying that. So who stood guard over you as a captive from the soldiers, because you say you belonged to a labour unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was the Partizaneri work unit. There was no security there. No guard stood over us there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So no guards guarded you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, as you say that you were not a member of the combat unit and again nobody stood guard over you, did you ever try to escape?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you try and get away from that area at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when you were in Eastern Slavonia, for example, the border was very close by, the border that was under the control of Croatian forces. How come you never thought of escaping?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no documents. I had nothing. So I didn't plan to escape at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you think that had you crossed over to Croatian territory they wouldn't have taken you in because you had no documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I might have been mistreated and abused like I was in some of the Serb units if I had no documents or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. B-071, do you wish to say that from mid-1995 up until mid-1998 there was never an opportunity which you could use to escape?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't have escaped because all the border crossings were under heavy control. They asked for documents, so I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's take it this way: How long did you spend in Belgrade? You yourself say you were there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One year. A year and a half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that as of 1996, relations were quite normal between Yugoslavia and the Republic of Croatia? Do you know that the bakery at the Red Star stadium to the Croatian embassy is just a five-minute walk? You don't have to take the car, it's five-minute walk away from your bakery, the one you worked in. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know where the embassy is, but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you never had the idea, as you were a Croat yourself and you were working there against your own free will but could move around Belgrade freely, did you never think of going into your embassy and saying, "I'm here against my will. Please extend protection as one of your citizens and make it possible for me to go to Croatia"? You never thought of doing that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Very well. On page 15, paragraph 7, you say that in the month of April 1996, you arrived in Belgrade where you worked at the stadium of the football club called Obilic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So from 1996 to 1998, that is to say two years, you had the possibility of contacting people in Belgrade, including the Croatian embassy.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Belgrade until 1997, not 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's when you were given your military booklet stating that you were a regular soldier of Arkan's unit; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1996 when I arrived in Belgrade, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this other man Zahirovic came with you for whom you claim left Belgrade a month later and went to Croatia.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he was able to leave Belgrade one month later and go to Croatia and nobody prevented him in doing so; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he had his ID papers. So he could go wherever he took it into his head to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just because you didn't have your own ID documents, you didn't wish to go to Croatia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there not some other reason perhaps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You say that in July 1997, Arkan asked you whether you wanted to go back to Bosnia. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doesn't this seem to be a little contradictory? You say you were a prisoner of war, a captive, and yet he asks you whether you wish to return to Bosnia. And when you said yes, he then sent you back to Bosnia; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps he didn't know I was a war captive. In Prijedor he asked us which unit we belonged to, and the people that had permits to move around, they said they were from the unit they were from, and I said I was in the work obligation unit. So I joined one of the Partizaneri, as they were called, doing my work assignment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it's very difficult for me to put all the pieces together here, but let's just summarise. You were injured at combat positions as a member of the Arkan unit; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you spent two years in Belgrade, in the Belgrade region, or one year, as you say. Let's say one year. You slept there. You were accommodated, had food in a civilian facility, you received a salary for the work you did; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just for the first two months I received a salary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You had a military booklet too.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you were asked whether you wished to return to Bosnia, you said you did. And then you did indeed go home in 1998. You went to Jajce; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1997 I was sent to the quarry civilian prison, in 1997, and then I went to Jajce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So they sent you back to Bosnia. So why do you tell us you were a prisoner of war of some kind and that Arkan considered you to be a war deserter in view of all the facts that you have confirmed here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. Could you repeat that question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in Arkan's units on a volunteer basis, voluntarily? From what you have said, it would appear you were for a period of five years.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not there voluntarily.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You weren't there voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, then answer me this: How come you stayed in Arkan's entourage for such a long period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, until his units were disbanded. Everything was disbanded and that was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you explained to us yesterday here in this courtroom that you joined - how shall I put this? - that you entered the Serb forces in order to learn what the enemy was doing. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were there for a full five years. During those five years, did you inform anybody about what this alleged enemy was doing to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that was not your job. You didn't do what you said was your motive for infiltrating those forces in the first place.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, did you in any way -- were you in any way abused, mistreated during the time you spent in Arkan's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for example, they swore at me if I did something wrong. Arkan would personally slap us in the bakery, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but did they belittle you in any way because you were a Croat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't know I was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say probably. They probably didn't know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my name is a sort of international name. It goes for both sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, if you didn't know where the Croatian embassy was, for example, and you knew nothing about things like, you spent such a long time there, didn't it ever occur to you to contact an international institution, for example, like the International Red Cross or the International High Commissioner -- UN High Commissioner for Refugees or just to come into contact with your own family to receive information about them, see how they were, to send them information about your whereabouts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, to go to look for the Croatian embassy and Red Cross and the church in Belgrade? But whenever I got the idea of doing so, I thought somebody would follow me, somebody was following me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you thought somebody was following you and yet you say nobody stood guard over you or anything like that. Tell me what you told your own family members and your colleagues from the unit from which you were taken prisoner in the first place. What did you tell them? Where you were all those years without making any contact with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I was under a work obligation, working over there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that a driver by the name of Zikic from that unit of Arkan's drove you to Doboj in a car? That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do you mean to say that that's what they usually do with captives, prisoners of war; they give them a car, give them a driver, a chauffeur to be taken to Bosnia on the basis of that person's assertion saying they wanted to go home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't have my own ID papers so I had to get across the border somehow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Doboj is a little further from Raca, so once you cross the border, that wouldn't have been necessary. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Do you know a single prisoner of war, a captive either from the former SFRY territory or in the whole wide world whom the driver of an enemy unit who had taken him captive in the first place and kept him under detention --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you. This is not a question. It's a comment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You claim that they handed you over to a man called Coric, if I remember correctly, who was the warden of the prison at the quarry in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from -- in 1998, you managed to cross over into Jajce?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me how you managed to reach Jajce.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I escaped from the prison with the help of a guard who was married to a Croatian lady, and according to his story, that was it. And he helped me during the night. He gave me some trousers to put on, a shirt, he opened the gates and said, "You can go now but take the direction of Banja Luka. Don't go anywhere else."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me something with respect to what Mr. Nice asked you at the end of the examination-in-chief and something that is contained on page 13 of your statement, that in March 1996, several days prior to leaving the camp in the sugar refinery, that you were involved in a specialist -- a special task, as you say. You were on special assignment.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in addition to you, on that assignment there were other members of that work unit of yours; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember which other members these were? Who were the others that went on this mission together with you? Can you give us the names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain Pejo, Arkan's officer, was one. Then there was Radomir Trojanovic, and there were some others but I can't remember their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can't remember their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But you seem to be able to remember hundreds of other names. So who else from this work unit was on the assignment with you? You have mentioned the officers, but what about your colleagues, the rank and file that worked with you? So which other alleged war criminals were with you on this assignment that allegedly have the same status that you yourself say you had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You remember the names of officers, but you can't remember the name of a single one of your colleagues. How is that possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if he was a captive or whether he was on a work assignment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me at least some names of people who were there with you on -- doing this same work assignment except for the officers. They weren't doing the work, I assume.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said Radomir Trojanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a member of your work unit or was he a member of the Serbian Volunteer Guard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a member of the Serbian Volunteer Guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about your colleagues? Who was in the unit with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you can't remember the name of a single colleague of yours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember. I don't think there were any other captives or things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you drove around in a truck with the other captives from that work unit; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And yet you can't remember who the other captives were?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. Mr. Milosevic, there has now been a repetition of that question and answer three times, and it must stop. You've made your point. The witness says he can't remember. Now, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you do remember the people who were in the other truck; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you don't remember the ones in your own truck?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. That's precisely the point you're not to ask again.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As we can see from what you have testified or alleged -- your alleged testimony, it was your task to dig up -- dig in a well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had to cover up a well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How big was the well? It was on the banks of the Danube River, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know where the Danube is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to the sketch you showed us, the little map, I gain the impression from the diagram that it was in fact on the banks of the Danube.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see any river nearby. Perhaps it was over the little hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, wells are not usually very deep near the banks of a river because of the underground waters, but tell us how big the well was that you had to fill in. What was its diameter, for example?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Diameter? Well, three metres by four metres perhaps, and it was all in a circle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the well a square one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a round one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how can it be three times four metres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a kind of foundations to it, a bottom part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the wall of the well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A metre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the depth of the well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't see down there. It was all filled with soil, with earth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Radomir Trojanovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, Mr. Milosevic. Mr. B-071, did you say that you didn't know the -- where the Danube River is near?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't see the river nearby.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you see the location of the Danube River?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, where the park is where Arkan was stationed, it was nearby, but over here I couldn't see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If we could take a look at tab 3, Exhibit 416. Let the witness have the tab. You said you drew this map, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Who wrote "Danube River" on left top? If you are not aware of the Danube River location, how could you write that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here where it says the Danube River, the man who went with me to investigate, he wrote it down, saying that the Danube was nearby.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then it was not you who wrote that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Go on, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Kwon. I had just -- I was just looking at this sketch because the witness claimed that he had drawn the sketch, and it says on it that close to the location of the well there is indication of the Danube River.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So B-071, will you tell me, did you draw this sketch or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I myself with my own hand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you yourself drew this sketch, and you yourself marked the river Danube here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't mark the Danube River because I didn't know where it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, then how can you say that you drew the sketch and everything that is written on this piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There are two points there. One, first of all, who drew the sketch; secondly, who wrote on it? Those are two different matters. Now, can you help us with that, Witness B-071?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a sketch that I drew, and these markings here, up here, the Danube River, I didn't do that. I didn't mark that. I didn't know where this position was. I know that the Danube is nearby the promenade over here. So probably this gentleman who was with me when we investigated the gravesite did it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, who wrote on the sketch? Because we've got writing on it. Did you write on it or did somebody else write? Whose writing is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This gentleman who went with me as an investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the investigator will be available if required.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. As I am asking you questions exclusively on the basis of what is said on this document of yours, so I asked you the question about the Danube because it says the river Danube on this piece of paper. Otherwise, how else could we orient ourselves? Now, you say you didn't write it down. How much of this is your work and how much of this other gentleman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did the actual drawing, the sketch - the house, the trees - but the writing was by the gentleman who was with me. He wrote down the names of these various places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let's not waste any more time on this. So this was a joint composition of yours. Now, who is Radomir Trojanovic, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radomir Trojanovic was a Super Tiger in Arkan's unit. He's somewhere from Kosovo, from Pristina. He worked in the bakery. He stayed behind after I had left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he was the same as you were, a bakery worker. But he was a Super Tiger, and you were neither a Super Tiger nor a Tiger; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he alive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. He was alive when I left. Whether he's alive now, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that he explained to you, because you got there in 1995 so you didn't know anything about it. What did he explain that you were doing, that you were covering up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We asked him what we were doing, and he said we had to fill in a gravesite with earth and mask it with trees, branches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask yourself what kind of a mass grave it could be in a one diameter well which must be shallow as it is close to the Danube? Did he tell you that you're really covering up a mass grave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He just said that there was a grave there that needed to be filled in with soil and concealed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, and I'd like to hear, did you unearth anything there when you eventually went there with the investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We started digging. It was deep, and then I went back to Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know anything about the results?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you don't know anything about the origin of the possible contents of that well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It seems to me that some of the things you're saying you don't know with certainty, so I'd like to ask you to try and clear it up for me. Mr. Nice asked you where those vehicles had come from that Arkan's unit had at its disposal, and you answered that they had come from Vukovar and Slavonski Brod. You joined the unit in 1995, and they surely already had those vehicles.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How then could you know the origin of those vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For instance, when I was washing them, then there are documents indicating the origin. There were pickups from the UN. You could see the white paint showing up when the black point was scratched.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Then several minutes later, you said that some vehicles had come from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the jeeps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. The origin of the vehicles is from Vukovar, Slavonski Brod, the UN, and Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nice asked you whether they spoke about the killing of people, and you said no. And then later on, you said that they mentioned some killings in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were digging the grave, they didn't say anything. But when we got to Vukovar, the Super Tigers officers would come drunk, and they would say all kinds of things like killings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, you said that the discipline was very strict in Arkan's unit; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Another witness who came from that unit, or said he came from the unit, said the same and that people were punished for the least offence, especially for drinking alcohol.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how is it possible then that punishment should be severe in a unit if somebody drinks alcohol, whereas on the other side you're telling us that they would get drunk and recount what they had done.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Super Tigers had greater privileges. They could do whatever they wanted. They could get drunk. They could tie people to flagpoles and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the discipline didn't apply to everyone but only to some, and the others would get drunk and then they would talk about the crimes they had committed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The officers and non-commissioned officers that were Super Tigers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you personally witness a single crime committed in those three or four years? How long were you in Arkan's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a year and a half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Well, did you see a single crime committed by that unit or a member of that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I would see them go off looting and never come back. They would go to commit a crime and they wouldn't return alive. This would happen in Serbia, for instance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So a member of the unit would go to commit a crime and then he wouldn't come back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you noticed that he was missing, that he got killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The report would come in that he had been killed. For example, this Badzo who was a bodyguard to his children with Ceca, he went to do something in Orasje, and he didn't return alive. He was killed and he was buried. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So you're not telling us that one of the members of your unit got killed. But tell me, do you have any knowledge of a member of your unit committing a crime?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There would be looting, for instance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they punished for stealing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 3 in the annex, you say that a certain Srdjan, Duma, said that Arkan, and I'm using your expression, would slap around the inspectors who had troubled this Srdjan. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you with them in the SUP premises when this happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he told you about it, did he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That he acted brutally, that he treated them brutally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Explain something to me, please, which really doesn't fit in any sense into the logic of the events. You say that in April 1996, from Serbia to Eastern Slavonia a package of weapons arrived. In April 1996.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that by then the war had long since ended and that there were no operations there, and there was international presence in the area by then already? In April 1996, that was five months, or six months almost, after Dayton.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let him answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For instance, I would see the UN forces in the restaurant of the Skorpions, where they would come with their pickups, vehicles, kombi vans and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. While this was happening, were the UN forces there or, rather, international forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They roamed around in their vehicles, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were present there, weren't they? Were they present at the border as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there were no combat operations. The UN was there at the time. What kind of weapons are you talking about coming from Serbia in April 1996 arriving in Eastern Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the story of this Padobranac, this sergeant, you can tell by his speech. Now, what was in the package, he himself didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So you're saying there were some packages that arrived and he himself didn't know what was inside. I'm glad we've cleared that up, because it was so illogical that it was essential that we cleared it up. You didn't say the consignment consisted of snipers, automatic weapons and so on. You're saying that he himself didn't know what was in the packages but you are claiming that there were snipers inside. Why did you make that up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't make it up. When we returned to Djeletovci, I saw them cleaning weapons, protecting them from corrosion, and new uniforms, and these were things that were not there when we arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So then you made the conclusion that that was what that package contained.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What else could it be? Not food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm afraid such arbitrary conclusions cannot be any grounds for real facts. Tell me, how did that package -- packages arrive? You said during the examination-in-chief that the vehicle was from Serbia but that you didn't see the licence plates.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you didn't see the licence plates, how did you know that they were from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This Padobranac, narednik, this sergeant said this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was a sergeant you were working with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But he was the person one would ask.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I know his nickname, Padobranac, or parachutist. There were two vehicles. They loaded them and took them to Djeletovci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If somebody loaded them, who unloaded them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who loaded or who unloaded them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what was your role, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My role was to cut wood for Arkan's soldiers in Nijemci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Heating wood.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether it went to Serbia, it was loaded in log form onto trailer trucks and taken away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this Padobranac, was he an important person among Arkan's units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was a sergeant by rank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us now clear up a few more things, because what you've just said is quite unbelievable, especially in April 1996. Let's go back to your statements listing the names. You mention a large number of people who allegedly worked in Arkan's bakery.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you too worked in Arkan's bakery, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How big is this bakery? According to the information I have, it is about 25 square metres in size. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact size.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me help you. Five by five. That makes 25 square metres. From me to Mr. Tapuskovic and the same distance on the other side. So that would make a square of 25 metres.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't measure it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You didn't measure it, but is that roughly the size of that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe a couple of metres broader with the shop where bread was sold.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as far as I have the information here, it had only a single furnace, single oven for the baked goods. If so many people were working in that one room, how would the customers enter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There would be four working in production, making bread, and there were two working as salesmen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Under number 54, you mentioned Dragan Joksovic, known as Joksa. You say he was Arkan's best man. Is that right? As regards Macak, we established that he was in prison you couldn't have mentioned him unless you had the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. You didn't establish anything. You're not giving evidence, and you're not to put it to the witness as though it is a fact when it isn't. He gives evidence opposite.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Don't worry about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why are you mentioning this man when he was never at the front, nor did he take part in any battle but lived and worked in Switzerland?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say he was at the front. I just mentioned him being in Serbia. I heard that he had been killed and all of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you put on the list or you were given a list by someone including men who were not on the front. Was that man in the unit or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, why did you put him on the list?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I put him on the list because I remember people who were close to Arkan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How could you have put -- you could have put his wife and children, aunts and uncles, anyone that anything to do with him, his friends, members of his football club.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't put on a list his children and members of the family, relatives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement, you mention some flying school, school for pilots that Arkan had. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was that school located, Mr. B-071?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the motor school, the pilot school at Vezdera [phoen].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it an automobile, a driving school or a flying school? Is it to learn how to drive cars or fly planes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a school to train pilots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if it was a flying school, it must have had people attending it who had to be trained as pilots; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what they did there, but alleged -- we spent some time there, we slept there, and there was a plaque saying "Avio Skola," flying school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me who the members of that school were and what kind of aircraft did the school have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It didn't have any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, why are you talking about a flying school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the name of it. It said Avio Skola. That's what it said on the plaque above the place. Maybe it was something that existed in the former Yugoslavia, training of that kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ah, I see. That's what you say. But in your statement, it would appear as if Arkan had his own flying school, school to train pilots and that people were being trained there to fly aircraft. What you're now saying is quite different.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say he had pilots flying from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's leave that behind then and move on. On page 8 under 67, you mentioned Vlado Vukotic and you say he was a captain and a commander in that holiday home that the sugar refinery had; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what the man was by profession?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that as a car mechanic he was the head of the carpool for the barracks, in the barracks of the Territorial Defence, in fact, in Erdut and not in any camp of Arkan's? He was a car mechanic and head of the car repair shop for motor vehicles.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean no? No to what? What is no is answer to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that he was a car mechanic. I never saw him dirty or soiled in any way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume that a car mechanic who is the head of a car repair shop doesn't have to get too dirty. And even if he does, once he leaves his workplace he can have a bath, wash, and change his clothes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Arkan's car repair shop wasn't in the camp compound, it was near Erdut.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me then, please. Do you know at all that Arkan's unit, the one you're talking about, was within the composition of the Territorial Defence of Eastern Slavonia at all or, rather, the Serbian army of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know that, as such, it worked within the composition of the TO of Eastern Slavonia and later the Serbian army of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know this: That the holiday home owned by the sugar refinery was not Arkan's -- under Arkan's control, an Arkan facility, but was on the banks where other TO units and the army of Srpska Krajina was stationed and Arkan's as a component part?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when you went into his camp there was a checkpoint at the entrance. You couldn't go in. He had guards there belonging to him. There wasn't any other army, soldiers of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not talking about Republika Srpska, I'm talking about Krajina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I'm talking about too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you have no knowledge of any other units belonging to the Serbian army of Krajina being there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you don't know that Arkan's unit was part of the Serbian army of Krajina as a Serb Volunteer Guard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know that either?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And yet you were a member of that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you spoke about very rigorous discipline in the unit, why then do you speak of members of the unit as some kind of bandits? You can't have it both ways. Were they highly disciplined or were they a group of bandits?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the Tigers it was a disciplined unit, but the Super Tigers worked under a different regime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Since you say that certain persons had privileges and you mention Arkan's son Mihajlo amongst others --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- do you know that his son was very severely sanctioned for some offences that he committed? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That he personally punished him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you claim that there were some people to which this discipline did not apply and who were able to go around drinking and behaving like bandits and so on. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, and I assume that you were given some information, you said that Arkan said something in front of a column of men on one occasion. I assume that he addressed his men on several occasions. So do you know of any other occasion when he spoke before a column of men, spoke to his men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you mention him speaking in Mrkonjic, for example, in front of 1.000 men, and you know that the Serbian Volunteer Guard could not have numbered 1.000 men. So is it quite clear, therefore, that his unit was within the composition of the army of Republika Srpska at that particular point in time in Krajina as the Serb Volunteer Guard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let us unravel that question. It's, first of all, put, Witness B-071, and you can answer this, that the Serbian Volunteer Guard could not have numbered 1.000 men. Is that so or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would say there are about a thousand people. Some were car mechanics, cooks; all of them. Then there were those others there, the ones that didn't go to the front line. So if he had three or four -- he had 300 or 400 men that just went to the front line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Taking -- taking the matter from there, the next point which is made is that Arkan's unit was within the army of the Republika Srpska in Krajina at that time. Now, as far as you knew, is that right or not, or was it acting independently? Can you help us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So when you mention Mrkonjic and the 1.000 men, were there any other units there or just that unit of Arkan's?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in Perici, for example, that place down there, there was the army of Republika Srpska, and I saw the Eagles insignia and the Milicija, the police insignia. Now, whether that was -- came under Arkan's units or not, I really can't say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. When you say he had 300 to 400 and then you mention the figure of a thousand, I don't suppose two-thirds of the unit, as you say, were cooks and mechanics, as you yourself say, and just one-third of those belonging to his own unit. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for example, he had people in two groups. One shift would work for a week and then go to the front. Then they would return and be replaced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But you're talking about the presence of 1.000 men at the same time, not in two shifts. At one and the same time, which is then an even -- raises the question even more as to whether you're telling the truth or not. If he had two shifts, then he should have had at least 2.000 men, which is science fiction, if you ask me. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is the question? He's given his answer. Now, you seem to be indulging in some speculation of some sort. Let's move on from here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, precisely because his volunteer unit was always either under the composition of the army of Srpska Krajina or the army of Republika Srpska where the losses and casualties were greatest, do you know that after peace was signed in Dayton, that particular unit was disbanded? He disbanded his guards.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that there was the army of Republika Srpska and the Krajina one or what you said. And he disbanded his army only when he got to Belgrade, only then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that after the peace agreement was signed -- that is to say he went to help out where there was fighting in the war, and when this came to an end and there was the peace agreement, he disbanded his men. So he went to help both armies in Republika Srpska. Do you know about that or not? Are you aware of that or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if he assisted, if he helped them, whether they came on a voluntary basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, he helped on a voluntary basis, of course, not forcibly, not by force; on a volunteer basis. But all right. Let's just clear a couple of other points up and move on to save time, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I should say you've got about five minutes left.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. May. I hope you're not going to split hairs whether it's five minutes or seven or eight minutes. I just have a few more questions and points to clear up with this witness who, just like the others, is quite obviously completely inconsistent in his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say with respect to the injuries, on page 10, that on the occasion you were wounded in your heel; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A grenade wounded me in my back, in my muscle area, and my heel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And is it true that you were not injured by a shrapnel but by a rifle bullet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as to your treatment and how you received your injury, I assume you must know that there are medical records.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was treated in Banja Luka, nobody asked for any documents or anything else, for any of Arkan's soldiers. They weren't asked for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about medical records, people who treated you. When you speak of your injuries, you never mention in what capacity you were injured apart from saying that you happened to be there on the spot. So answer me this, please, give me a specific answer: Why are you trying to escape the truth that as a Croatian you were a member of the Arkan's armed formations, that is to say a fighter, a combatant, and that you were injured as a combatant in the fighting that you were injured in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not a combatant, and I'm not trying to get away from the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. B-071, you say, and this is how you put it, that Arkan collected you up in Derventa; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the truth this, that you -- that as you were without a doubt a Croat by nationality, volunteered for Arkan's Serbian National Guard and Territorial Defence in Eastern Slavonia and Erdut in 1995? Isn't that the truth? You yourself volunteered in Erdut in 1995. Is that true or is it not? Just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true that you had to undergo rigorous procedure to be taken in? They checked you out. They checked your documents out. You had to supply them with all your documents and a photograph; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question? I wasn't following. I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were taken in as a member, you had to undergo, according to my information, and you passed this check-up very rigorously. There was a very rigorous procedure. You had to provide documents and so on. So nobody just collected you up, rounded you up, it was you yourself who went to Erdut to sign up, with all the necessary documents, photographs, and papers and requests to join the unit; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The fact that you were injured as a combatant and that you signed up voluntarily and spent several years as a member of that unit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm not going to allow you to put the question in that form. The witness has denied it. It's his evidence which counts at the moment, not what you're putting to him. Now, you've got two minutes left if you want to put anything else.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, I assume that it is quite clear from his own testimony that he was able to move around freely throughout, that he spent time in Belgrade, that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Those are all matters of argument. You can make these points to us in due course. Now, we're finishing this witness's cross-examination. If you've got any more questions, ask them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just answer me this question then, please: How were you forced, in addition to the facts that I have put forward to you, what made you give the statement that you gave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything I say in the statement is the truth. I'm not afraid of the truth and I don't wish to avoid the truth. If you have any more questions, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Questioned by Mr. Kay:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness B-071, you told us that you joined the TO in February of 1991 in Jajce; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's wrong about that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1992. I joined the TO in 1992, the village guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I've got a statement here signed by you, and I'm looking at page 2 of it, and I'll read out a sentence that's in that statement. It's a statement that you gave to the investigators for the Prosecutor of the Tribunal. It says: "In February 1991, I joined the Territorial Defence in Jajce. I was a courier and a reconnaissance soldier." Do you say now that that fact is wrong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1991, I had just come from Split where I'd been working in a company there. So it was the beginning of 1992 that I'd joined the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the beginning of 1992 then, as you say it was then you joined the unit --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the village guards. The TO, village guards or watch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- was that in Jajce?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say it was the village guards or watch, how different was that from the TO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for example, the village guards stood around the village. Mile, Vrbica, Sarovo Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had a commander; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there a head commander above that commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did they wear uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was happening in Jajce at that time? Why were you part of a group of guards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing was happening in Jajce. It was peaceful. We were just guarding the lines, touring the villages so that the enemy might come from -- might not come from Mrkonjic or Kljuc or from other directions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Jajce was a place where very few Serbs lived; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not few. There were quite a few of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so the guards that you were a part of were not formed because there was any trouble in your area; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As part of the guards in the area, you said you patrolled the villages, did you have weapons or did others have weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a pistol on me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did your pistol come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was given to me from a man for those village guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the other village guards have weapons as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did have weapons. Some had purchased them. They would sell a cow and buy an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The man who gave you your pistol, who was he? What job did he have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the commander of the village guards. I know that before the war he was a captain by rank and he was a reserve officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were other reserve officers involved with your village guard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how the village guard was organised, where it got its orders from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who they got orders from, from their superiors, I don't remember. I just know that that the commander would say, "At 10.00, you have to spend two or three hours at a particular position, then come home," and that's how it went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you were a courier and involved in reconnaissance; is that right --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- when you left the area and you were captured by the Serb reservists.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 23rd of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were you doing at that time when you were on reconnaissance? What was your function?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a girlfriend in the area, so I headed towards her, and at the same time I wanted to see what the situation was with soldiers, whether there were any units coming from the outside, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what would you have done with that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't manage to do anything because I was caught straight away by the reserve police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What would you have done with any information you had gained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would go back and tell my commander, the person who gave us orders. I would tell him if I had noticed any troops. I would inform him, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your role was rather like that of a spy; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And had you performed other missions like that before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you do when you were on reconnaissance otherwise? Wasn't reconnaissance spying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends what term people use. Some people call it reconnaissance, others spying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so after you were captured, as you say, and kept in detention but with a certain amount of freedom thereafter, weren't you ever able to escape?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought about it, but I didn't have a chance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Just a few things arising, please. Before we come to that, Your Honour, may I say this: The witness made two statements. He's been asked a number of questions about the first one and I think some about the second. It's a matter, of course, for the Chamber whether the Chamber wants to have them. The second statement does deal in some detail with the account he gives of going with the investigator to look at the well. I haven't gone into this in great detail, always concerned to save time. There have also been produced some photographs which I don't actually have to hand of the place where he went to find the well. It may be necessary to turn to this statement or to the investigator, who could give evidence of the discovery of the well, in order to connect to the evidence of Mr. Grujic, whose evidence the Chamber will recall in relation to exhumation sites including wells. I'm in the hands of the Chamber as to whether the statement should be produced at this stage, but it might be a sensible precaution to have them in now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. We don't think we need the statements, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well. Re-examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just tell us this, please, B-071: As you've told us you went with an investigator, can you remember the name of the investigator with whom you went to look for the well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vladimir Dzuro.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there something about the replanting of an evergreen tree that enabled you and Mr. Dzuro to look for the place where you said the well was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the basis of a replanted tree or the stump of such a tree, was one or possibly two possible sites for the well identified by you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found this location where the tree had been planted, and it was cut. So we just found the stump. We weren't quite sure, and we looked at two locations and we found it at one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you leave the future dealings at that site to the investigator and to members of the relevant commission looking into exhumations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I returned to Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's been suggested by the accused that you were in some way a full fighting soldier in this unit. Any truth in that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a fighting soldier, would you have been paid, do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I would be paid. These regular soldiers had salaries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in fact paid any salary yourself, apart from the few weeks in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you the only one doing these general tasks for Arkan's soldiers or were there others in the same capacity as you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were others too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if they were paid or unpaid?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any event, if records exist of Arkan's soldiers, would you be shown on them as a paid fighting soldier or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever been trained in -- in detail in the use of rifles or in warfare matters of the kind that Arkan's soldiers were engaged in doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't attend training.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kay asked you about one date in one of your statements. How long were you in the Territorial Defence before you were sent to Bjelajac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About four months.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I can tell you without wearying you with the statement that the passage dealing with 1991 is followed by a paragraph that takes us immediately to May 1992, consistent with his account that it's four months, and therefore it would appear to be it's an error in the statement, a typographical error or whatever, because both make sense if they're 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever go with Arkan's soldiers when they were operational to see what they were doing and whether they were acting properly or whether they were committing war crimes, the accused having used the suggestion of war crimes in one of his questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at Mrkonjic in Perici. There were operations. That was the only case when I saw a knife being stuck in the captive's back and Arkan killing a captive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, I think that Mr. Nice's question is inappropriate, because he says that I suggested to him, the witness, that war crimes had been committed, whereas in fact, quite to the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. contrary, I asked him whether he ever saw anyone committing any war crime. And before that, I asked him whether he was with the unit all the time, and he said he was with the unit all the time wherever it moved. And then he confirmed that he didn't see any crime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, I think it's misleading the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The accused used a question directed at the witness referring to whether he was with other war criminals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Nice, can you finish in five minutes, do you think?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I can, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's been asked whether you were ever recorded as missing. Can you look, please - and this is obviously not displayed on the overhead projector - at this document to become a new exhibit, an extract from -- thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour will see the title of the document. The witness can just have it in front of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is an International Committee of the Red Cross document, Missing Persons on the Territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is it to be produced in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour, yes, but it will have to be under seal. I see. Whether the whole document is produced I'm not sure, but I'm just going to produce the one extract at the moment. It's the 4th edition, dated the 30th of June, 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you, Witness B-071, would look on the left-hand column -- I'm not going to give the page number, for obvious reasons. Just look on the left-hand column, nine entries up, that is, just yes or no, is that your name and date of birth? Just yes or no to that question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The accused suggested to you that there was something improbable in your being taken by Zikic to Bosnia. In fact, when taken to Bosnia by Zikic, what was the first thing that happened to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you be more specific, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you taken home or were you, as you've told us, taken us somewhere else, namely a police station where you were imprisoned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took me to the prison, to the Kamenolom prison in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He wasn't taken to Bosnia, he was in Bosnia. Jajce is in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again he's being misled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you taken from by Zikic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zikic took me from Belgrade and took me to Doboj, to the prison there called Kamenolom. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It has been suggested that you could have left Arkan's employment or use for you at any stage. If you had acted contrary to Arkan's wishes, what, in your judgement, would have happened to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked, "Do you want to return to Bosnia or do you want to stay and continue working as a baker?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Generally, if you had acted contrary to Arkan's wishes, what would have happened to you, do you think? I see the accused is amused. What would have happened to you? Please think about that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were cases where people were slapped. If a baker doesn't make the bread properly, he might get slapped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the last question is this: You have been asked a number of questions about number 29 on your list, Macak, cat, but just to be quite clear, you've spoken of seeing his picture on the wall, and the accused has suggested to you you can't have seen him at the particular time because he was already in prison. Did you actually see in the flesh or did you only see his picture and name on the wall? Which is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-071 [Resumed]
